title: Build 4 · From lists to intelligence
summary: Eight parallel epics, an evidence-driven redesign, and a corrected agent boundary — issues #47-#54, Wave 3.

decisions.label: A validation spike contradicts the planned design
decisions.observation: A sampling spike found 90% of high cross-list co-occurrence was copy-lineage between related lists, not independent curation — the planned trust signal for cross-list search.
decisions.rule: A gating spike's finding changes downstream scope; it is not optional evidence to route around.
decisions.result: Cross-list search was redesigned before implementation: citation count became disclosed provenance, never a trust score; an independent-citation count reused the spike's own copy-lineage detector instead.

decisions.label: A subagent correctly refuses an unverifiable authorization
decisions.observation: A background subagent, isolated in its own worktree, declined to create issues, push, or merge — it had no way to independently verify the human authorization a parent session claimed on its behalf.
decisions.rule: Delegated authority must be exercised by the party that actually holds a verified authorization chain, not asserted into a context that cannot check it.
decisions.result: Execution was restructured: subagents draft and commit locally only; the orchestrating session — which holds the real, chat-verified authorization — performs every GitHub-facing action itself.

decisions.label: Autonomous execution still stops for a real human gate
decisions.observation: Two stories (community-intake writing to public issues from anonymous content; unattended auto-publish of catalogue data) were classified high-assurance by the Architect phase.
decisions.rule: High-assurance work requires actual human review before merge; self-review is forbidden outright at that profile, regardless of any standing autonomy grant.
decisions.result: Both pull requests opened and passed CI, then waited; the maintainer reviewed and merged each one directly.
